hook: AHRP: a lady plays a golden HARP while a seal next to her claps and barks "ARP! ARP!": ARP
kohn-truh-BAHS: a woman plays the tall DOUBLE BASS while a fat BASS fish leaps from a bucket beside her: BASS
bah-GEHT: a schoolgirl on the podium holds a conductor's BATON in one hand and a long loaf of BAGUETTE bread in the other: BATON = BAGUETTE
shehf dor-KEHSTR: a CHEF in a tall white hat stands on the podium and conducts with a wire whisk: the CHEF (= boss) of the orchestra
ahr-SHEH: a boy dressed as an ARCHER draws a violin BOW like a bow and arrow at an apple: ARCHER
vee-yoh-LOHN: a man sits on a lawn chair (a LAWN) on a little patch of grass and plays his VIOLIN: LAWN
ahl-TOH: a barefoot man plays the VIOLA, pointing at ALL his TOES: ALL-TOE. Note: English "alto" is a voice; French alto is the viola.
note: viola (string instrument); English "alto" is a voice range; false friend: not a singing alto; French alto = viola

hook: vee-yoh-lohn-SEHL: a young man on a stepladder plays a big CELLO, a VIOLIN so big it needs a CELL of its own: VIOLIN-CELL
klah-ree-NEHT: a girl plays her CLARINET while her brother holds a butterfly NET: CLARI-NET
oh-BWAH: a man on stage plays the OBOE with a green BOA snake coiled around him and gasps "oh, BOA!": oh-BOA
bah-SOHN: a man on a stool plays the BASSOON while a little lamb beside him goes "BAA": BAA-SON
sak-soh-FOHN: a girl in a sack race plays a SAXOPHONE standing inside a burlap SACK: SACK
KOR: a boy plays the French HORN and holds up an apple CORE: CORE. Also a corn (hard lump) on the foot.
note: also a horn; watch corn false friend
